descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-92586 AC 7-8; UAT TC-07 ER 5 · “Handoff can only be sent to a signed-in, valid recipient, not an arbitrary email address”. Mixed: stated part — handoff reaches the recipient, retrievable by both, self / non-account refused; our part — empty-text refusal, third-party read refusal and audit rows (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Approach · TC-07 Task Export · S18 Existing specs: the Handoff delivery and record that Send reuses

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T3 The Handoff delivery that Send reuses: in-app only, to a signed-in valid account (never yourself, never an address), recorded with sender, recipient and timestamp, retrievable by both and by nobody e … (TFA-92586 AC 6; TFA-92586 AC 7; TFA-92586 AC 8) — gate: blocked: TFA-92586 ready for pr

Test design technique: Equivalence classes (equivalence) — Check the same rule again with another class of input (Hospital / Nursing Home, other data); every class has to be right.

Given Two accounts (DEMO_USER, OTHER_USER) signed in through the API

When List recipients; send a handoff; read it as recipient and sender; try self, a non-account and empty text; read as a third party

Then Picker lists other accounts by id and name only, never the caller; the handoff reaches the recipient with sender name, is retrievable by both, audited; self / non-account / empty are refused; a third party cannot read it

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Playwright API assertions. They pin the Handoff side of 'same delivery and record as Handoff'; they send a handoff, not a task list, so they are no evidence for U7/U8 (S16, S17)
